description: We aim to build an interactive web tool for NASA’s Planet X and SPHEREx challenge, making infrared sky observations easy to explore and compare over time. Using real NASA data, Python, image processing, and data visualization, we hope to highlight potential moving or changing objects. We welcome teammates passionate about astronomy, AI/ML, scientific data analysis, and web development.
summary:
SPHEREx Analysis of 3I/ATLAS
Our project uses NASA's SPHEREx mission data to study the interstellar object 3I/ATLAS. We developed a website that presents scientific observations, visualizations, and analysis of the object's characteristics using SPHEREx survey data.
The project helps users explore astronomical data, understand image processing techniques, and compare observations to identify important features. We also implemented image analysis and PSF comparison to improve our understanding of the observational data.
Our goal is to make complex astronomical data easier to explore and understand through an interactive, student-developed platform.
details:
Project Details

Our project, SPHEREx: Student Analysis of 3I/ATLAS Survey Data, is a web-based platform developed to explore and analyze NASA SPHEREx observations of the interstellar object 3I/ATLAS.

The website presents scientific information, observational data, image visualizations, and analysis results in an understandable and interactive format. We developed image-processing and comparison techniques to study SPHEREx data, including Point Spread Function (PSF) analysis, QR2-to-QR3 image resampling, and effective PSF (ePSF) validation. These techniques help us examine image quality, pixel alignment, and differences between processed observations.

Our platform aims to make astronomical data easier for students, researchers, and space enthusiasts to explore without requiring advanced knowledge of astronomical data processing. It connects scientific analysis with accessible visual explanations, helping users understand how space telescope observations can be studied.

We developed the project using Python for scientific data processing and analysis, and HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the interactive website. We also used scientific image-processing scripts and visualization tools to examine and compare observational results.

The creative aspect of our project is combining real NASA mission data, scientific image analysis, and an accessible web interface into one platform. During development, we considered data accuracy, image quality, calibration, pixel alignment, scientific reliability, usability, and clarity of presentation.

Our intended impact is to encourage students and the public to explore real astronomical observations and develop a better understanding of interstellar objects and space science through NASA data.
